subject: Licensed residency & snapshot protocol — on‑prem addendum negotiation
messages:
From: Emma Carroll <emma.carroll@cedarhealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Licensed residency & snapshot protocol for private hosting

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week — Cedar Health leadership asked me to follow up on two deployment items before we progress the SOW: license scope for on‑prem/operator residency, and an auditable snapshot protocol for quarterly compliance checks. Our legal team would like clear wording in the MSA/addendum that covers:

- what parts of the model and weights are "licensed" versus delivered for customer custody;
- whether Redwood can retain an immutable snapshot for disaster recovery and how access is controlled;
- an escrow‑like mechanism for audit (third‑party attestation preferred);

I've attached our MSA request form and a short compliance checklist. Can you send any existing addendum language or a proposed runbook?

Also looped procurement: procurement@cedarhealth.com for timelines.

Regards,
Emma Carroll
Sr. Procurement Manager
Cedar Health Systems
[Attachment: Cedar_MSAA-Request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
To: Emma Carroll <emma.carroll@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensed residency & snapshot protocol for private hosting

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Appreciated.

High level: we support a private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment model where production weights remain under a limited license; customers can opt for operator custody snapshots. For audit/escrow, we have two standard paths we typically propose:

1) Escrow‑lite: periodic blinded snapshots (hashes + metadata) with a third‑party attestation under NDA.
2) Full snapshot custody: a secured snapshot handed to the customer or custodian with access controls and an operator runbook.

I'm attaching an initial draft addendum and a first version of our snapshot runbook so you can see the operational controls. Laura — can you review the license boundary language? Priyom — can you confirm implications for order form pricing if Cedar elects full snapshot custody?

Next step: would you prefer a 30‑minute legal/technical review next week?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RINF_onprem-addendum-draft.docx]
[Attachment: snapshot-runbook-v1.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensed residency & snapshot protocol for private hosting

Alex / Priyom — reading the request and the draft addendum. Initial legal notes:

- License boundary: we should define "Model IP" (weights, architecture, optimizations) and "Operational Artifacts" (config, KV cache) separately; the MSA should grant a limited, non‑transferable license to the customer for production use but reserve core model IP to Redwood.
- Snapshot custody: prefer escrow‑lite as default (hashed snapshots + attestation) unless customer needs on‑site custody for regulatory reasons. If Cedar requires full snapshot delivery, we will need:
  * a signed custodian agreement;
  * indemnity carveouts for operator‑performed maintenance;
  * a narrow, time‑boxed access window for audit.
- Evidence for audits: propose a 3‑tier evidence package (attestation report, access logs, hashed snapshot manifest).

I'll draft redline language for the addendum (license + custody exhibit) and push it back by EOD Monday. Priyom — we should also capture pricing delta for custody/transfer.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
To: Emma Carroll <emma.carroll@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed addendum + snapshot runbook (redlines attached)

Emma — attaching our consolidated redline and a slightly expanded runbook that outlines the operational steps if Cedar elects escrow‑lite versus full snapshot custody. Highlights:

- Escrow‑lite (default): Redwood will generate quarterly cryptographic hashes of snapshots, retain a timestamped manifest, and provide a third‑party attestation report on request. No live weights are handed over; logs and access metadata provided.
- Full snapshot custody (optional): we can encrypt and transfer a snapshot to an agreed custodian. Transfer includes a transfer verification procedure and a one‑week staging window. Pricing: one‑time transfer fee + ongoing custody fee (see attachment 'redlines‑initial.pdf' for placeholders).

Next actions I propose:
- Short legal sync (30m) to walk through the addendum language — suggest Wed 13th or Thu 14th PT
- Procurement to confirm acceptance of transfer fee model so we can update the order form

Attachments: redlines‑initial.pdf (redline addendum), snapshot‑runbook‑v2.pdf (runbook).

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines-initial.pdf]
[Attachment: snapshot-runbook-v2.pdf]

From: Emma Carroll <emma.carroll@cedarhealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@cedarhealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jun 2028 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed addendum + snapshot runbook (redlines attached)

Alex — thanks for the fast turnaround and helpful detail. A few clarifying questions from our security and procurement teams:

1) For escrow‑lite, can you explain what the third‑party attestation covers? Is it a review of process only, or will it include sample restore verification?
2) For full custody, does Redwood have a standard custodian you work with, or do we nominate our own?
3) Procurement: can we get a firm quote for the one‑time transfer fee and a monthly custody rate to include in the order form? We need that to complete internal approvals.

Also procurement flagged a SOC 2 evidence requirement — can you point to the folder or provide a timeboxed package?

If it's helpful let's take the 30m sync — we are available Wed 13th 11:00 PT / Thu 14th 09:00 PT.

Best,
Emma
[Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 13 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed addendum + snapshot runbook (redlines attached)

Alex / Laura — quick internal follow up after Emma's questions:

- Attestation scope: third‑party attestation will cover process controls and a limited restore test (one sample restore) — we'll confirm the attestation provider and scope with the customer.
- Custodian: Redwood has preferred custodians we can propose (we'll share contacts) but Cedar may nominate their own custodian subject to a standard security questionnaire.
- Pricing: preliminary numbers — one‑time transfer USD 12,500; monthly custody USD 1,200. I'll run these through pricing to confirm and update the order form draft.
- SOC2 evidence: link to our standard evidence package included below. We should share a timeboxed bundle (30 days retention) to procurement.

Plan: confirm pricing and attestation scope in the sync tomorrow, then Alex can provide a DocuSign link for the addendum + order form.

Priyom Das
Head of Deployment Ops, Redwood Inference
